title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit/Open
plain: The engine computer can't properly control the EVAP leak detection pump, which pressurizes or pulls vacuum on the fuel vapor system to test it for leaks. It sees an open or broken circuit, often from wiring, a connector or the part itself.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Blown fuse or bad relay feeding the circuit

checks: Inspect the leak detection pump connector and wiring
Check for power at the connector and measure the part's resistance
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the EVAP leak detection pump.
examples: Leak detection pumps like this are used on many Chrysler, Dodge and Jeep vehicles

title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit Low
plain: The control circuit for the EVAP leak detection pump is reading low voltage. This part pressurizes or pulls vacuum on the fuel vapor system to test it for leaks. A wire shorted to ground or a shorted part is the usual reason.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Internally shorted EVAP leak detection pump

checks: Check the leak detection pump wiring for rubbed-through insulation
Measure the leak detection pump resistance and compare with spec
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the EVAP leak detection pump.
examples: Leak detection pumps like this are used on many Chrysler, Dodge and Jeep vehicles

title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit High
plain: The control circuit for the EVAP leak detection pump is reading high voltage. This part pressurizes or pulls vacuum on the fuel vapor system to test it for leaks. A wire shorted to power, an open circuit or a failed part is the usual reason.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Control wire shorted to a power source

checks: Check the leak detection pump wiring for shorts to other wires
Measure the leak detection pump resistance and compare with spec
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the EVAP leak detection pump.
examples: Leak detection pumps like this are used on many Chrysler, Dodge and Jeep vehicles

title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit/Open
plain: The engine computer has found a problem in the circuit for the EVAP leak detection pump sense circuit, which reports back to the computer whether the leak detection pump is working. It usually points to wiring, a connector or the sensor itself.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Inspect the leak detection pump connector and wiring for damage or corrosion
Check the sensor power, ground and signal with a meter
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the EVAP leak detection pump.
examples: Leak detection pumps like this are used on many Chrysler, Dodge and Jeep vehicles

title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The EVAP leak detection pump sense circuit is giving readings that don't make sense compared with what the computer expects. This sensor reports back to the computer whether the leak detection pump is working. The sensor may be failing or the system it watches may have a real problem.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Failing or out-of-calibration EVAP leak detection pump
Leak detection pump stuck, or a blocked or leaking EVAP hose
High resistance in the wiring or connector

checks: Compare the leak detection pump reading with related sensors in live data
Check wiring and connector for corrosion or looseness
fix: Confirm the system itself is working, then replace the EVAP leak detection pump if its readings are off.
examples: Leak detection pumps like this are used on many Chrysler, Dodge and Jeep vehicles

title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Low
plain: The signal from the EVAP leak detection pump sense circuit is lower than the computer expects. This sensor reports back to the computer whether the leak detection pump is working. A wire shorted to ground or a failed sensor is the usual reason.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Signal or reference wire shorted to ground

checks: Inspect the leak detection pump wiring for rubbed-through or pinched spots
Unplug the sensor and see if the reading changes, which helps separate wiring from sensor
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the EVAP leak detection pump.
examples: Leak detection pumps like this are used on many Chrysler, Dodge and Jeep vehicles

title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit High
plain: The signal from the EVAP leak detection pump sense circuit is higher than the computer expects. This sensor reports back to the computer whether the leak detection pump is working. An open (broken) wire, a bad ground or a failed sensor is the usual reason.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Open or broken signal or ground wire
Wire shorted to a power source

checks: Make sure the leak detection pump connector is fully plugged in and clean
Check the sensor ground and signal wire for an open circuit
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the EVAP leak detection pump.
examples: Leak detection pumps like this are used on many Chrysler, Dodge and Jeep vehicles

title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
plain: The signal from the EVAP leak detection pump sense circuit keeps dropping out or jumping around. This sensor reports back to the computer whether the leak detection pump is working. A loose connection or a damaged wire is the usual reason.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Chafed wire that opens or shorts as the engine moves

checks: Wiggle the harness and connector while watching live data for dropouts
Inspect the leak detection pump wiring along its whole route
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the EVAP leak detection pump.
examples: Leak detection pumps like this are used on many Chrysler, Dodge and Jeep vehicles

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation System Performance
plain: The EGR system, which feeds a little exhaust back into the engine to lower emissions, isn't flowing the way the computer expects. Carbon clogging is the most common reason.

causes.name: Faulty EGR position or pressure sensor

checks: Inspect and clean the EGR valve and passages
Command the EGR valve with a scan tool and watch engine response
fix: Clean the EGR valve and passages; replace the valve if it sticks or fails testing.

title: O2 Sensor Exhaust Sample Error Bank 1 Sensor 1
plain: The front oxygen sensor on bank 1 (the side of the engine with cylinder 1) is seeing outside air mixed into the exhaust, so its reading isn't accurate. An exhaust leak near the sensor is the usual reason.
symptoms: Possible ticking or puffing sound from an exhaust leak

causes.name: Exhaust leak near the front oxygen sensor (manifold, gasket or flex pipe)
Oxygen sensor not threaded in fully

checks: Check for exhaust leaks around the manifold and front pipe
Make sure the sensor is tight and its threads are sound
fix: Repair the exhaust leak; replace the oxygen sensor only if it still reads wrong.

cost.job: Repair exhaust manifold or gasket leak

title: O2 Sensor Exhaust Sample Error Bank 2 Sensor 1
plain: The front oxygen sensor on bank 2 (the side of the engine opposite cylinder 1) is seeing outside air mixed into the exhaust, so its reading isn't accurate. An exhaust leak near the sensor is the usual reason.
symptoms: Possible ticking or puffing sound from an exhaust leak

causes.name: Exhaust leak near the front oxygen sensor (manifold, gasket or flex pipe)

checks: Check for exhaust leaks around the manifold and front pipe

fix: Repair the exhaust leak; replace the oxygen sensor only if it still reads wrong.

title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 1 Sensor 2 / Bank 1 Sensor 3
plain: The computer thinks the sensor 2 and sensor 3 oxygen sensors on bank 1 are plugged into each other's connectors. This usually happens after one is replaced.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Trace each sensor's wire to the correct connector
Review any recent exhaust or sensor work
fix: Plug the sensors into the correct connectors and clear the code.

title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 2 Sensor 2 / Bank 2 Sensor 3
plain: The computer thinks the sensor 2 and sensor 3 oxygen sensors on bank 2 are plugged into each other's connectors. This usually happens after one is replaced.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Trace each sensor's wire to the correct connector

fix: Plug the sensors into the correct connectors and clear the code.

symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Blown fuse or bad relay feeding the circuit

checks: Inspect the EVAP switching valve connector and wiring
Check for power at the connector and measure the part's resistance
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the EVAP switching valve.

title: Evaporative Emission System Switching Valve Control Circuit Low
plain: The control circuit for the EVAP switching valve is reading low voltage. This part routes fuel vapor in the evaporative emissions system. A wire shorted to ground or a shorted part is the usual reason.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Check the EVAP switching valve wiring for rubbed-through insulation
Measure the EVAP switching valve resistance and compare with spec
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the EVAP switching valve.

title: Evaporative Emission System Switching Valve Control Circuit High

title: Evaporative Emission System Vent Valve Stuck Open
plain: The EVAP vent valve, which seals the fuel vapor system during leak tests, seems stuck open. The system can't seal and test itself.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Dirt or debris holding the vent valve open

checks: Command the vent valve closed with a scan tool and check that it seals
Inspect the valve and its filter for dirt or spider webs
fix: Replace the vent valve and clean or replace a clogged vent filter.

title: Evaporative Emission System Vent Valve Stuck Closed
plain: The EVAP vent valve seems stuck closed, so the fuel vapor system can't breathe. You may notice trouble filling up the tank.
symptoms: Fuel pump nozzle clicks off early when filling
Possible whoosh of air when opening the fuel cap
Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Clogged vent valve filter or vent line (dirt, mud or spider webs)

checks: Inspect the vent line and filter for dirt, mud or insect nests
Command the vent valve open and closed with a scan tool
Check if the fuel tank holds pressure or vacuum it shouldn't
fix: Clear any blockage and replace the vent valve or canister if needed.

title: HC Adsorption Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 1
plain: A special catalytic converter on bank 1 (the side of the engine with cylinder 1) that stores unburned fuel (hydrocarbons) during cold starts isn't working as well as it should. This part is used on some low-emission vehicles.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Worn or damaged hydrocarbon trap catalyst
Engine misfire or oil burning that damaged the catalyst

checks: Check for misfire codes and exhaust leaks first
Check sensor readings related to the catalyst
fix: Fix any misfire or leak first; a worn catalyst must be replaced.

title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Too High Bank 1
plain: The exhaust on bank 1 (the side of the engine with cylinder 1) is getting hotter than is safe. This can damage the turbo, catalytic converter or particulate filter.

causes.name: Engine overfueling or a leaking injector
Clogged particulate filter or exhaust restriction

checks: Check exhaust temperature sensor readings against each other
Check for exhaust restrictions and leaking injectors
fix: Fix the cause of the high exhaust heat, such as a leaking injector or clogged filter; replace the sensor only if it reads wrong.

title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Too High Bank 2

checks: Check exhaust temperature sensor readings against each other

fix: Fix the cause of the high exhaust heat, such as a leaking injector or clogged filter; replace the sensor only if it reads wrong.

title: Diesel Particulate Filter Restriction - Ash Accumulation
plain: The diesel particulate filter has collected so much ash (left over from burned oil additives) that it is restricted. Unlike soot, ash can't be burned off, so the filter needs cleaning or replacing.

causes.name: Normal ash buildup in a high-mileage filter
Engine burning oil, adding extra ash
Faulty DPF pressure sensor or hoses

checks: Check DPF pressure readings with a scan tool
Check for oil consumption
fix: Have the filter professionally cleaned or replaced, and fix any oil burning.
examples: Seen on high-mileage Ram Cummins and GM Duramax diesels

title: Secondary Air Injection System Air Flow/Pressure Sensor Circuit Bank 1
